messages:
Mae SRE: heads-up — over the last 20m we've seen a flurry of DNS resolution failures to the headless service model-infer-edge in us-west-edge after a couple of spot GPU preempts. Symptoms: client connects time out or gets an IP that immediately drops 502s.
Raj Infra: can you paste the failure pattern? which pods/nodes affected?
Mae SRE: saw spike in 502s from the routing layer, attached traces show kubernetes service discovery returning empty endpoints intermittently. observed right after node preempt events.
Sam Runtime: noticing the same on the metrics side — endpointslice count for model-infer-edge temporarily drops then slowly repopulates. looks like endpointslice-controller doesn't prop the new slices fast enough when pods reschedule.
Carlos Eng: any coredns errors? often see NXDOMAIN if caches get weird.
Mae SRE: here's tail of coredns logs at the time:
```
[INFO] 2026-03-18T18:12:02Z lookup: model-infer-edge.default.svc.cluster.local -> 0 answers, cached=false
[WARN] 2026-03-18T18:12:04Z upstream timed out
```
Raj Infra: also check kube-proxy mode on those nodes (ipvs vs iptables). IPVS will accept endpointslice updates faster but if conntrack entries point to an evicted node you can hit blackholes.
Sam Runtime: kube-proxy on preempted nodes shows stale rules for ~30s in our logs. suspect conntrack entries aren't being removed quickly enough.
Carlos Eng: cpuload on control-plane at the time? controller-manager backlog?
Mae SRE: control-plane CPU looked spiky — saw burst of scheduling + endpointslice controller logs complaining about apiserver 429s for a few seconds. might be cascading: spot preempt -> pod reschedule storm -> controller clients rate-limited -> endpointslice updates delayed -> kube-proxy/conntrack inconsistencies -> client 502s.
Raj Infra: that chain makes sense. quick mitigation: reduce pod churn on preempt by setting pod disruption budgets / graceful termination? also increase endpointslice-controller burst / qps if safe.
Sam Runtime: actionable fix we can try now: 1) bump endpointslice-controller leader election to increase QPS (temp). 2) set kube-proxy conntrack ttl lower so stale entries expire faster.
Mae SRE: agree. also adding a short readiness delay on model pods would avoid flipping endpoints during heavy restart storms.
Carlos Eng: any correlation with the canary we rolled 18:10? deploy-bot: canary rollout model-serving v2 started at 2026-03-18T18:10:00Z to us-west-edge (10%).
Mae SRE: good catch — the canary triggered extra scheduling as it pulled images onto spot nodes that were getting preempted. that amplified churn.
Raj Infra: I'm going to temporarily pause canary and increase endpointslice-controller QPS to 50. Sam, can you draft the kube-proxy conntrack TTL patch for a rolling restart?
Sam Runtime: will do. suggested kube-proxy args: --conntrack-ttl=10s and --conntrack-min=1000 (testing). will schedule a small-canary restart on 2 nodes first.
Carlos Eng: also suggest adding node readiness delay for preemptible node groups so we don't schedule hot pods immediately.
Mae SRE: action items: (1) Raj pauses canary (done), (2) Raj bump controller QPS, (3) Sam roll kube-proxy change on a couple nodes and watch, (4) Carlos open PR for readiness probe + pdb adjustments for model-infer deployments.
Oncall Bot: incident created: INC-2026-314 — "headless svc discovery lag after spot preempt". Priority: P2.
Mae SRE: postmortem TODO: look at apiserver rate limiting thresholds and whether we can mitigate with client-side backoff in controller. also evaluate affinity/anti-affinity to reduce co-locating critical pods on spot nodes.
Raj Infra: rolling change applied to endpointslice-controller config (QPS=50) at 2026-03-18T18:22:00Z. monitoring for resolution.
Sam Runtime: kube-proxy restart canary started on node us-west-edge-spot-23 at 2026-03-18T18:30:00Z. preliminary metrics show conntrack stale entries cleared faster.
Mae SRE: 18:40 — errors falling back to normal. marking as mitigated, leaving incident open for follow-up.
Carlos Eng: will prepare a short doc with recommended defaults for preemptible pools to avoid this recurrence.
Mae SRE: thanks all :thumbsup:
